title.en: The Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles

text.en: Every Indian school begins its day with the Preamble: 'We, the people of India...'. It is the opening promise of the Constitution and tells us what kind of country India wants to be.

The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which we celebrate as Republic Day.
The Preamble declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
Fundamental Rights are the basic rights of every citizen: right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
Right to constitutional remedies lets a person go to the High Court or Supreme Court if a right is violated, so Dr Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the government to build a welfare state; they are not enforceable in court.
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) are duties of citizens, such as respecting the Constitution, the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment and developing scientific temper.
The Constitution has a Preamble, many Articles grouped in Parts, and Schedules; it can be amended by Parliament by a defined procedure.

problem.en: A person's property is wrongly taken by the government without law. Which right helps them, and where do they go?

text.en: Right to constitutional remedies protects other fundamental rights.
They can file a petition in the High Court or the Supreme Court.
The court can order the government to correct the wrong.

why.en: That is how a right is enforced.

prompt.en: What are Fundamental Rights and how do they differ from Directive Principles?

requiredIdeas.en: Directive Principles are guidelines, not enforceable

points.en: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
The Preamble: sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.
Six Fundamental Rights are enforceable in courts.
Directive Principles guide the government; duties guide citizens.
